quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Nebraska's speed law requires you to drive:

options.text: Five miles per hour above the posted speed limit.
At a speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that is safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Nebraska law requires you to drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, but not faster than the posted limit. Slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: If you change your name or address, you must apply for a new driver's license within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 60 days.
questions.explanation: You must apply for a new license within 60 days of changing your name or address. You can apply at a Driver Licensing Office or online for address changes.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic control, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, then go.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Release the gas, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: The minimum legal speed on an interstate highway is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 mph.
questions.explanation: The minimum speed on interstate highways in Nebraska is 40 miles per hour. Only drive slower if conditions require it.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You may not follow a fire truck responding to an emergency closer than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Keep at least 500 feet behind a fire truck responding to an emergency. Do not park within one block of where the fire truck has stopped.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter the street, you should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right of way.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down entering the curve, speed up leaving it.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up entering the curve, slow down leaving it.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down entering the curve, speed up leaving it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: It is legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You may never exceed the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn sharply.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to run into the street in front of your car. This can help warn them of danger.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings. All drivers must obey them.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck open while driving on a busy street. You should:

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, your car will keep going fast even when you lift your foot. Turn off the ignition carefully. Move the ignition switch just enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: Which of these are used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for different purposes. They tell you whether to go straight or turn.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot go in that direction.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, the driver on the right should insist on having the right-of-way.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not insist on your right-of-way. Always let other drivers go if it can prevent an accident.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a car with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically, faster than you can do it by hand.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines on streets and highways are used to:

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: At an intersection with a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to check for any cars you may have missed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Making a right turn here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: You can never turn left at a red light.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a red light in one situation: when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. There must be no sign prohibiting the turn. This is the only time a left turn is allowed at a red light.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could hit your vehicle.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep moving without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could hit your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicles crossing or merging that are close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: The correct way to exit a freeway is to:

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Once on the ramp, then reduce your speed.

questions.question: You can turn left at a red light after stopping only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Check that no sign prohibits this turn.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not expect the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
Expect the other driver to let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Expect the other driver to keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expect the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that the space you want is open or that other drivers will give you the right-of-way, even if you use your turn signal.
